title: Random forest prioritizes investigational compounds with antiplasmodial activity
summary: A random-forest classifier screened investigational compounds; after applicability, similarity, diversity, availability and cost filters, six compounds were purchased and tested. CEP-37440 and AZD-1480 had reported P. falciparum IC50 values of 1.22 and 4.00 µM. These are in-vitro findings for existing compounds, not evidence of malaria clinical safety or a confirmed parasite target.
organization: Birla Institute of Technology and Science Pilani; Institute of Bioinformatics and Applied Biotechnology

evidence.tested: Primary article reports tested CEP-37440/AZD-1480 antiplasmodial activity.
evidence.unknown: Selected six are filtered, not a random sample; proposed parasite kinase mechanisms and patient efficacy are unverified.
evidence.ai_role: RF ranks investigational compounds from a drug database; human filters determine purchase/assay set.

source_review.scope: publisher primary full text. Material checked for the specific claims stated in the record.
